title: Apple’s stock flirts with bear market after Guggenheim cuts rating
text: #1 1 hour ago Shares of Apple Inc. tumbled toward a four-month low on Wednesday, after Guggenheim Securities analyst Robert Cihra cut his rating and earnings estimate, saying rising selling prices is “no longer enough” to offset weakening iPhone units. The stock AAPL, +2.47% dropped 2.8% to the lowest price since July 5. That took Apple’s market capitalization below $900 billion for the first time since May. The shares extended their losing streak to five sessions, and have shed 11.0% during the streak, contributing to a 19.5% loss since the Oct. 3 record close of $232.07. At Wednesday’s intraday low of $185.93, the stock was 19.88% below its record close. Many on Wall Street define a bear market as decline of 20% or more from a bull-market high. A close at or below $185.656 would mark Apple’s first bear market since August 2016. The selloff comes as Wall Street has become increasingly concerned about falling iPhone demand, after smartphone components suppliers Lumtentum Holdings Inc. LITE, +5.74% and Qorvo Inc. QRVO, +3.63% warned this week of lower-than-expected sales. Late Wednesday, supplier AMS AG AMS, -0.90% cut its revenue outlook because of “recent demand changes from a major consumer customer.” The warnings confirmed fears that unit sales could slow, after Apple said it would no longer provide unit-sales figures
